lines.text: Former President of the United States of America

Former President of the United States of America · Experience: White House · Location: Washington · 500+ connections on LinkedIn. View Barack Obama’s profile on LinkedIn, a professional community of 1 billion members.
Washington, District of Columbia, United States

James Baldwin’s The Fire Next Time shaped the way I saw the world as a young man. I sat down with Ta-Nehisi Coates to talk about what Baldwin meant to both of us when we first encountered his work, and what his ideas about race, power, and creating change can still teach us today. I hope you’ll listen to our conversation on my podcast, A Great Book with Barack Obama, now on Audible.
Happy anniversary, @MichelleObama! I’m still the luckiest guy in the world to be with you.

When @MichelleObama and I were thinking about how to maximize our impact after leaving the White House, we landed on the idea of creating mentorship programs at the @ObamaFoundation. We wanted to invest in leaders around the world, just like people invested in us — helping them embrace broad perspectives, harness collective power, and drive meaningful change. We’re excited to introduce you to this year’s cohorts for our Obama Leaders Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe, and USA programs. Some of them are students trying to find their place in the world, others are already on their way, with careers that span government, business, and civil society. But all of them have a shared commitment to create positive, sustainable change in their communities and around the world. They join the members of our Voyager Scholarship with @BChesky and Obama Foundation Scholars program with the University of Chicago, and we can’t wait to see what they do!
Congrats to my @WhiteSox (and @Cubs) on making the playoffs! Let’s ride a hot streak all the way to the World Series.

I’ve always believed that the right book at the right time can change the way you see the world. At least that’s what they’ve done for me. For my new podcast from @HigherGroundMedia and @Audible, A Great Book with Barack Obama, I chose six books that have stayed with me over the years and invited a few friends who have their own connections to these stories. We talked about everything from faith and fatherhood to race, power, friendship, and what it means to grow up. More than anything, these conversations reminded me why I love reading in the first place — and I hope they do the same for you. Check out A Great Book available now only on Audible.

Yesterday, we lost a cherished member of our family. We got Sunny at the start of our second term in the White House, and all of us – including our first dog, Bo – immediately fell in love. We also had trouble keeping up with her, for Sunny was a force of nature. Athletic and full of boundless energy, she leapt over the hedges on the South Lawn like they weren’t even there, chasing squirrels, birds and anything else that moved. And whereas the way to Bo’s heart usually involved a treat, Sunny was more interested in having us run around with her, roll on the floor with her, or have her belly rubbed for as long as we were willing. She loved the girls, even if they were pestering her when she was napping. She loved our team, and would often follow them around, helping them on the job. She was fiercely protective of Bo, who she rightly sensed wasn’t always as alert and attentive as she was. She had her eccentricities: other than Bo, she preferred people to dogs; she was a loud and sloppy drinker; and despite being a Portuguese Water Dog, she hated getting wet. But as far as our family was concerned, she was pretty much perfect, and for thirteen years, she would be by our side – always loyal, always sweet, always ready for adventure, still fiery and gorgeous till the very end of her days. We will miss her terribly, and imagine she’s with her big brother now, making sure he’s okay.

If you were young in 2001, or weren’t even born yet, it can be hard to imagine what 9/11 felt like. The shock of that beautiful, cloudless morning. The heartbreak of the families whose loved ones were taken with such swiftness and cruelty. The realization that the forces of malevolence and violence were closer, and the future less certain, than we knew. But in the days that followed, we felt something else, too. Pride in the rescue workers who had rushed to the scene, and the passengers who had stormed the cockpit. Admiration for the men and women who left behind lives of comfort to serve their country. A deep resolve that nothing would break the will of a truly United States of America. Today Michelle and I are remembering those we lost that day, and those who made the ultimate sacrifice in the wars that followed. We pray for their families. And we hope Americans everywhere remember the true lesson of 9/11: that we can survive even our darkest days as long as we move forward as one nation and one people.

Toryn Parks, a union roofer, spent months atop of the Obama Presidential Center Forum and Museum buildings, pouring hot tar and meticulously laying weatherproofing layers, roll by roll. Recently, she walked the campus with her family to show them the work firsthand. “I’m a part of history now,” Parks said with a smile. “Going to trade school opened a lot of doors. It’s just surreal. I’m still making an impact right in my neighborhood.” This Labor Day, check out Toryn Parks’s story on Obama.org/stories.

Music has always had the power to connect and inspire us. At the opening of the Obama Presidential Center, @EddieVedder and the young people from @GuitarsOverGuns wrote and performed a profoundly moving song, ‘Better Believe’, that spoke to each of them and all of us. It is an example of what we will continue to do at the Obama Presidential Center — bringing people together, expanding their imaginations, and watching them create a little magic. Check out their story and incredible performance at the link in our bios.

Some people put their ideas out in the world and hope they catch on. Not Gloria Steinem. Through her writing, her speeches, and her organizing, she demanded that the world pay attention to all the ways that women had been — and in some cases, still are — treated unfairly. And she helped awaken us to problems like domestic violence, the lack of affordable child care, and unfair hiring practices that had too often been ignored or overlooked. Gloria really was larger than life. Today, generations of women are walking a little taller and aiming a little higher because of what she fought for and achieved. Michelle and I are thinking of her family today, and everyone — women and men — who were inspired by her towering example.

Earlier this year, President @BarackObama talked with some Obama Leaders about AI, and how to take advantage of the opportunities it provides while minimizing the risks. Oyungoo Enkhbold worked as an ethical AI and cybersecurity consultant at the United Nations Development Programme Accelerator Lab in Mongolia and is now studying for a master’s in public administration in development practice, with a focus on AI governance. She wanted to know how democratic leaders can harness AI without letting it become a tool to silence their own citizens. Jenny Romano is the CEO of The Newsroom, a Portuguese technology company building the infrastructure to trace claims back to their sources. She asked President Obama how people can use technology to build a movement for good. In both cases, President Obama stressed the importance of educating the public, building coalitions, and keeping the conversation going.

This summer, more than 50 young men from @chipubschools attended the @MBK_Alliance-Obama Leadership Academy to get ready for high school. They earned credits toward graduation, developed important life skills, and built connections. We’re so proud of their hard work, and can’t wait to see what they do.

latestIgtvVideos.caption: Michelle and I were lucky enough to know Her Majesty The Queen. Back when we were just beginning to navigate life as President and First Lady, she welcomed us to the world stage with extraordinary generosity. Our thoughts are with the Royal Family and those mourning her passing.

My mother, Ann Dunham, was the biggest influence on my life. She had a core belief in our common humanity, and she made sure I recognized the inherent dignity in every person. 

Today I’m proud to share that the Water Garden at the Obama Presidential Center will be named in her honor.

The Ann Dunham Water Garden will be a special place for visitors and members of the community to come together and reflect. It will also feature an incredible new sculpture by Maya Lin, whose work I’ve long admired. 

Thanks to the incredibly generous members of the Obama Alumni family who helped bring this project to life. I can’t wait for you to see it.

Ahead of Mandela Day, I spoke with the talented young people who just completed our @ObamaFoundation Leaders Africa program. They’ve been working on some of the most pressing issues across the continent, and are working together to find solutions. I couldn’t be prouder of them.

It’s not every day I get to wear a hard hat. Last week, I got to stop by the site of the Obama Presidential Center and was so inspired by the progress that’s been made and how this team is living up to the ideals we’ve set.

We’ve always believed that the people building the Center should look like the community it calls home on the South Side of Chicago. I’m proud that our team is recruiting and training people of color to be leaders in the industry—creating a new model for diversity in construction—and that we’re on track to meeting our ambitious goals.

Michelle and I started the @ObamaFoundation's Futures Series to connect the young leaders of tomorrow with the trailblazers of today. It’s great to see the impact that it’s already having on students from the South Side.

On World Refugee Day, we recognize the challenges that refugees face, honor their courage, and celebrate their contributions to our country. 
 
If you would like to welcome refugees as your neighbors, join @Welcome.US at the link in my bio.

We need to build democracy for the future—and what gives me hope is the promise and potential of the next generation of leaders coming up. In Copenhagen last week, I had the chance to meet some of those young folks working with the @ObamaFoundation.
For the 10th anniversary of DACA, I met with these inspiring young people who shared their stories, the impact that DACA had on their lives, and the work that remains to support them.

Tomorrow, I'll be speaking at the Copenhagen Democracy Summit. 

At a time like this, what gives me hope is the promise and potential of the next generation of leaders—who understand that democracy hangs in the balance and are ready to do what they can to save it. 

Take a look:

Michelle, Brian, and I all share the belief that connection enriches our lives by exposing us to new people and experiences. It’s why Michelle and I started the @ObamaFoundation — to bring together the next generation of leaders, help them build connections, and learn from each other. And it’s why we’re excited about the Voyager Scholarship, too. 

For so many young people who want to pursue careers in public service, money stands in the way. That’s why the Voyager Scholarship helps students by providing them with financial aid, meaningful travel experiences to expand their horizons, and a network of leaders to support them. 

Brian and I recently spoke with some young people about how the Voyager Scholarship will help students pursue careers in public service. Click the link in my bio to learn more about the Voyager Scholarship and apply by Tuesday, June 14.

Today, I’m joining those around the world in celebrating Her Majesty The Queen’s Platinum Jubilee. It is with gratitude for your leadership and the kindness you’ve shown me and my family that I say, may the light of your crown continue to reign supreme.

In 2009, Carlton Philadelphia, a National Security Council staffer, brought his wife and two sons to the Oval Office for a departure photo. Carlton’s older son, Isaac, asked me a few serious questions, but a more surprising one came from his younger brother, five-year-old Jacob. 

“Is your hair like mine?” he asked. 

It wasn’t the kind of question I usually get. 

So, I bent down and told him, “Well you want to check and see? Go ahead, touch it.” 

And then I asked him, “Well, what do you think?”

He replied, “Yeah, I think that’s pretty much what I’ve got. ” 

White House photographer @PeteSouza captured that moment and for years, the photo hung in the halls of the West Wing. It was a reminder of one of the reasons I first ran for president: that if I were to win, young people—Black kids, Hispanic kids, kids who may not have always felt like they belonged—might see more possibilities for their own future. 

It’s hard to believe 13 years have passed. Today, Jacob will graduate high school and continue on to the University of Memphis to study political science. And I couldn’t be more proud of him. We recently reconnected to reflect on that moment and his journey. Check out our reunion. 

Congratulations, Jacob, and best of luck to the Class of 2022!
